text:
maria: seeing repeated OOMs on ded-rt-prod-7 starting 2478901080, spike coincides with the autoscaler pushing up batch sizes after the kernel-selector tweak.
alex: timeline? any profiling traces? :thinking_face:
maria: profiling attached (summarized): kernel_selector chose new 'fast-attn-v2' path -> 20% higher ephemeral workspace per-token; continuous batching backlog increased, kv-cache warmups delayed -> memory pressure + late OOMs.
sourav: interesting — that kernel's memory footprint grows with seq_len^2 when we don't hit the optimized path; regression from commit 7f2a. quick mitigation: force conservative kernel on busy routes and reduce batching window.
olivia: agree. propose immediate mitigations we can apply without deploy: 1) route-level override to use `kernel_selector=legacy` 2) reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 4096 3) set kv-cache soft-ttl to 30s to free cold entries 4) enable request-throttle header for high-QPS clients.
maria: can you paste the route override? I can apply.
sourav: use this (route config patch):
```
PATCH /v1/routes/production/generate
{
  "runtime_hint": {
    "kernel_selector": "legacy",
    "max_batch_tokens": 4096,
    "kv_cache_ttl_secs": 30,
    "oom_circuit_breaker": 0.6
  }
}
```
ram: note: lowering `max_batch_tokens` will increase per-request latency slightly but should drop memory per-GPU.
deploy-bot: @maria requested a config patch to /v1/routes/production/generate. Starting canary application to 2 nodes.
maria: applying now.
oncall-bot: Alert suppressed for ded-rt-prod-7 while canary in progress. Incident ticket: INF-2026-129.
alex: while canary rolls, we should also flip allocator soft-reserve settings on that pool: `ALLOCATOR_SOFT_RESERVE=0.08` -> reduces reserved pool for big spikes.
sourav: exact command to flip env via kubectl:
```
kubectl -n inference set env daemonset/runtime-pool ALLOCATOR_SOFT_RESERVE=0.08
kubectl -n inference rollout restart daemonset/runtime-pool
```
olivia: also enable aggressive KV eviction sampling for that pool to reclaim cold prefixes:
```
PATCH /v1/admin/pools/runtime-pool
{"kv_eviction_sampling": "aggressive"}
```
maria: can we enable temporary request shaping to reduce tail latencies from clients sending huge contexts? suggest header `X-Req-Shape: conservative` mapped to `max_input_tokens=2048`.
ram: deployed header mapping via ingress: done.
deploy-bot: canary succeeded on nodes runtime-7a and runtime-7b; rolling to remaining nodes.
alex: after full rollout, watch these signals: GPU free memory 95th->50th pct, kv-cache hit rate drop < 10% is expected but should recover, tail latency <= +30%.
maria: post-mitigation status: OOMs stopped after 2478901268, there were 3 late failures during canary window.
olivia: follow-ups: 1) revert kernel change in next patch and add mem-regression test 2) add end-to-end perf regression alert for kernel_selector path diff 3) update our incident playbook with this exact rollout+allocator steps.
sourav: for the longer-term: add a sampling profiler on kernel selection to capture memory delta per selector, and wire autoscaler to respect peak workspace estimates instead of just avg tokens.
ram: noted. I'll open infra tasks and link to INF-2026-129.
maria: thanks all. leaving this thread as the incident write-up; will attach flamegraphs and the pprof links to the ticket.
olivia: :thumbsup: good job.
